title: Artin–Rees stabilizes the cohomology of actual adic quotient short complexes
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I$ an ideal, and $S=(M\xrightarrow{f}N\xrightarrow{g}P)$ a short complex of $R$-modules, meaning $gf=0$. Assume $P$ is finitely generated; $M$ and $N$ need not be finite. At level $n\geq0$ form the actual quotient short complex $S/I^{n+1}S$, with its canonical quotient transitions. The inverse system $H(S/I^{n+1}S)$ is Mittag–Leffler [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system]. Every additive exact functor between module categories preserves this property. In particular, for any small site $(\mathcal C,\tau)$ and object $U$, the functor $N\mapsto\underline N(U)$ of sections of the actual constant module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] is exact and carries this cohomology system to a Mittag–Leffler system.

source.place: Tag 09C5, last paragraph, with the direct cycle argument from algebra.tex Tag 00IN (lemma-Artin-Rees) replacing the Tor spectral-sequence calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to $\operatorname{im}(g)\subseteq P$. Choose $c$ with $I^mP\cap\operatorname{im}(g)\subseteq I^{m-c}\operatorname{im}(g)$ for $m\geq c$. If $m\geq n+c$ and $gz\in I^mP$, the image-of-submodule formula $g(I^nN)=I^n\operatorname{im}(g)$ supplies $y\in I^nN$ with $gy=gz$. Thus $z-y$ is a true cycle reducing to the same element modulo $I^n$.

Represent a cohomology class of $S/I^{n+c+1}S$ by a cycle and lift it to $z\in N$. The previous step replaces it modulo $I^{n+1}$ by a true cycle. Reduce that true cycle at any deeper level $t$; its image in level $n$ is the original class. Naturality of the kernel-to-cohomology quotient gives the same equality for the actual transitions. This is the eventual-range criterion for Mittag–Leffler. Identity transitions and repeated indices are literal quotient maps.

An inclusion of images $\operatorname{im}f\subseteq\operatorname{im}g$ is the equality $f\pi=0$ for $\pi$ the cokernel projection of $g$. An additive exact functor preserves this equality and the exact sequence of $g$ and $\pi$, hence preserves the image inclusion. Apply this to the stabilized ranges.

For constant-module sections use [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties] on the kernel sequence of every epimorphism to show that sections preserve epimorphisms. Constant sheafification, the sheaf inclusion and evaluation preserve finite limits, so the sections functor preserves homology. Apply the preceding step.

theorem isMittagLeffler [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R)) [Module.Finite R S.X₃] :
    (tower I S ⋙ forget _).IsMittagLeffler
